initiatives.title: A prototype that shows the whole mission
initiatives.why: Every kind of participant and every kind of help, on a phone, in the approved voice. The thing to hand someone so they get it in a minute.

initiatives.title: A backend that can run it for real
initiatives.why: Real data, real accounts, real matching. The prototype's flows, made durable.

initiatives.title: Trust
initiatives.why: Everyone here is who they say they are. Grants only reach confirmed organizations. No spam, no fraud.

initiatives.title: The public site
initiatives.why: Where the idea-giver and early partners see progress: prototype, design brief, how it works, this roadmap.

initiatives.title: The organization behind it
initiatives.why: Decisions that aren't code: the name, the entity, the platform, the partners.

initiatives.title: A working alpha for invited nonprofits
initiatives.why: Real organizations post real needs and offers, start threads, and make golden threads, on the map, on any phone or desktop. Target: live Sep 30.

epics.title: Direction on paper
epics.goal: Mission, voice, taxonomy, and app map written and approved before screens are built.

epics.title: The front door
epics.goal: Sign up through confirm for all six kinds of participant.

epics.title: Seed data from real sources
epics.goal: Schools, programs, foundations, people, needs, offers, grants, and one Together, generated from public data where it exists.

epics.title: The core loop
epics.goal: Board, a need or offer, post, thread, inbox: the same flow for six kinds of help.

epics.title: Grants
epics.goal: Confirmed organizations search grants and leave to apply on the funder's site.

epics.title: Directory and profiles
epics.goal: Find anyone here, joined or not; one profile layout for six shapes.

epics.title: The map
epics.goal: The picture of threads and golden threads, with fewer controls and a legend for six kinds.

epics.title: You
epics.goal: Your profile, your posts, how often you're seen.

epics.title: The story guide
epics.goal: Three short stories that each end on the map.

epics.title: The design page
epics.goal: The mission, the six kinds, the eight threads, and the decisions, in the voice, on one page.

epics.title: Data loads
epics.goal: Every list the app relies on arrives through a loader that produces one shape.

epics.title: Accounts and claiming
epics.goal: Real sign-in, one account per person, claiming an organization by kind.

epics.title: Mission features in the backend
epics.goal: Kinds of help, cadence, priority levels, fair ranking, tags, alerts, threads.

epics.title: Grants in the backend
epics.goal: Grant records, the eight filters, gating, and the hand-off link.

epics.title: A real map
epics.goal: Base map tiles and street-level geocoding of every address.

epics.title: Confirmation per kind
epics.goal: Each of the six kinds has at least one way to prove they belong, and a person reviews the rest.

epics.title: Spam and fraud
epics.goal: Rate limits, a review queue, reporting, and revocation.

epics.title: GitHub Pages site
epics.goal: Prototype, design brief, how it works, and roadmap, phone-first, rebuilt from the repo.

epics.title: Going public with the name
epics.goal: Replace Name TBD everywhere when the name is announced.

epics.title: Form the 501(c)(3)
epics.goal: The entity that runs this as a community-impact organization.

epics.title: Pick the platform
epics.goal: What the real app is built in, and the accounts it ships under.

epics.title: Integrations
epics.goal: Corporate giving and volunteering platforms, once there's something to integrate with.

epics.title: Accounts and invites
epics.goal: Sign in with Google; an invite code confirms you for one organization; anyone else waits for review.

epics.title: The core loop, working
epics.goal: Board, a need or offer, post, thread, inbox, backed by the real API.

epics.title: The map, for real
epics.goal: A real base map, every nonprofit as a dot, clusters, and threads that drift and glow gold when done.

epics.title: Live and invited
epics.goal: Hosted, installable, with privacy and terms, and 8 to 12 organizations invited.
